info.title: Adobe Brand Intelligence Simulate — MCP Tool Reference
info.description: The 8 Simulate MCP tools' request/response schemas. The internal tools `get_simulation_status` and `upload_asset_bytes` are excluded — they are called by the MCP-Apps progress and upload panels themselves, not by integrators. Adobe Brand Intelligence is an MCP server: every real call goes over a single JSON-RPC endpoint at /mcp, not per-tool HTTP routes. The per-tool `POST /tools/<name>` paths documented below are a DOCUMENTATION CONVENTION only — one synthetic operation per registered MCP tool, so a human reader can see each tool's request/response shape in a familiar OpenAPI/Swagger viewer. They are not callable HTTP routes: do not run client codegen against this document and expect the result to work against /mcp.

post.summary: ONE-TIME setup for Adobe Brand Intelligence — run this once per machine, when
post.description:
ONE-TIME setup for Adobe Brand Intelligence — run this once per machine, when
            the user first connects this server or asks to initialize / set up /
            install / update Simulate (or its skill). It installs the
            "new-simulation" skill locally. Not part of running a simulation, and
            not needed again afterwards: to actually test something use
            get_simulation_options / create_simulation / list_simulations.

            The skill teaches you the full simulation workflow. This server is
            remote and cannot write to the user's disk, so install it as a skill
            for your own host however you normally would.

            Inputs: none.
            Returns: skill_name, skill_document (the full SKILL.md), and message
            — a short line to show the user.
            Next: install skill_document as the skill named skill_name. Write it
            byte-for-byte, frontmatter included: a host ignores a skill file whose
            YAML frontmatter is missing, so a reformatted or summarized copy
            installs as an inert file with no visible error. Then report the
            message to the user.

schema.description:
The bundled skill's content, for the ASSISTANT to install.

The server cannot write to the user's disk, so there is no command to run
here — it returns the skill content, and the calling assistant writes the
file itself with its own file tools (it knows its own host's skills
directory; the server does not). How to do that is spelled out in the
tool's description rather than in the payload.

skill_name.description: The skill's name, which is also its directory name.
skill_name.title: Skill Name

skill_document.description: The full SKILL.md content, verbatim including YAML frontmatter.
skill_document.title: Skill Document

message.description: A short line to show the user. The install how-to is in this tool's description, not here.
message.title: Message

schema.title: SimulateInitResult

post.summary: Run or browse in the Adobe Brand Intelligence workspace — call this to get a
post.description:
Run or browse in the Adobe Brand Intelligence workspace — call this to get a
            workspace_id before creating or listing simulations. Pick the
            workspace yourself: default to the one flagged is_active (the
            workspace the user's Adobe Brand Intelligence app currently has open) — do NOT
            ask the user to choose. Only ask, or switch to a different one,
            when the user names a specific workspace or asks to switch.

            These tools ARE the Adobe Brand Intelligence app — operate it directly through them.
            When the user says "in / on the Adobe Brand Intelligence app" (or "the simulate
            app"), that is a request to use these tools, not to open a browser: do
            NOT launch a web browser or computer-use to drive the Adobe Brand Intelligence web
            UI. Use these tools instead.

            Returns: every workspace you can access, with its workspace id,
            name, kind ("personal" | "shared"), and is_active (True for the
            one to default to). Show the user the workspace name — keep
            workspace_id for the tool calls, don't surface it. Next: pass the
            chosen workspace_id explicitly to create_simulation,
            list_simulations, and get_simulation.

schema.description: ``list_workspaces`` result — a top-level object, not a bare array.
schema.title: ListWorkspacesResult

post.summary: The menu for a new simulation. Call this when you reach the
post.description:
The menu for a new simulation. Call this when you reach the
            TEMPLATE decision — whenever the user wants to run, test, evaluate,
            or compare anything with an audience ("run a simulation", "test 3
            names", "compare these taglines", "which option best fits the
            brand", "how will the audience react", "test two emails on the
            simulate app"). It lists the building blocks for the run;
            create_simulation cannot be called until you have.

            A simulation needs FOUR DECISIONS, settled in order: objective,
            assets, template, audience and participants. Ask ONE QUESTION AT A
            TIME, always offering options, and resolve a decision from what the
            user already said rather than asking when their ask already answers
            it. This tool serves the last two decisions (template, audience) —
            the objective and the assets come from the conversation, so do not
            wait on this call to start.

            This also covers asking-the-audience phrasings that never say
            "simulate": "which of these emails works better", "will this land
            with my customers", "gut-check this before it goes live", "how would
            our audience react", "review/compare these creatives", "be honest,
            does this feel generic". And role-play framings — "be the voice of
            the customer/consumer and tell me...", "be the customer in the room",
            "you are my Basics segment, which do you prefer". Those are NOT
            requests for your own opinion: do not answer them from your own
            judgment, do not invent ratings or scores, and do not rewrite the
            user's copy. Start here and let the synthetic audience be that voice.

            This IS how you run something in the Adobe Brand Intelligence app — call it
            directly. Do NOT open a web browser or computer-use to drive the Adobe Brand Intelligence
            Simulate web UI, even when the user says "in / on the simulate app";
            that phrasing means use this tool, not browse a page.

            Inputs: none.
            Returns: study templates (each with a title, a description, allowed
            design types, key questions, dimensions, and form defaults) plus the
            populations + segments you can target. When you show the user
            templates to choose from, give each one's title AND its description
            — the description is what says what the template measures, so a bare
            list of titles is not enough. Populations and segments are presented
            by name. Keep every id in context to pass to create_simulation.
            Next: pass a template_id, population_id, and segment_id(s) to
            create_simulation.

schema.description: get_simulation_options result — every choice a run needs.
schema.title: SimulationOptions

post.summary: The DEFAULT, primary way to collect LOCAL binary files (images,
post.description:
The DEFAULT, primary way to collect LOCAL binary files (images,
            video, html, audio, or an email body image) for an Adobe Brand
            Intelligence simulation, on ANY host — this is the tool to reach for
            first, not a last resort. It opens an inline panel for the user to
            pick files (drag-and-drop, multiple files); the bytes flow through
            the MCP connection itself, so it works even where the host has no
            shell or network egress. Use it whenever the user needs to supply a
            local file with no public URL. Do NOT open it for a text asset or an
            email's subject/preview — those are inline and never upload. Never
            ask the user to run an upload command or paste asset JSON
            themselves.

            Inputs: none.
            Returns: opens the panel; on a host that can't render it, returns
            instructions to use prepare_asset_upload instead.
            Next: after upload, pass the returned upload_id(s) to create_simulation
            inside the asset — a media asset as
            {type:"image", asset: {source:"upload", upload_id}}, or an email
            body image as {type:"email", subject, body_image:
            {source:"upload", upload_id}}. ``label`` is optional on every asset
            — omit it and the server auto-numbers "Option 1", "Option 2", ...

schema.description: This tool has no outputSchema — FastMCP returns unstructured text for it, not a structured JSON result.

post.summary: FALLBACK for staging a LOCAL binary file (a media creative, or an
post.description:
FALLBACK for staging a LOCAL binary file (a media creative, or an
            email body image) when open_asset_upload's panel cannot render on
            the connected host. Prefer open_asset_upload otherwise — it works on
            any host. Only reach for this tool when the host cannot show the
            panel AND can run shell commands itself (it needs a shell and
            network egress to run the returned upload command). Use this ONLY
            for Adobe Brand Intelligence simulations, and only for a file on the
            user's machine (for a public URL, pass it straight to
            create_simulation instead). Do NOT use it for a text asset or an
            email's subject/preview — those are inline and never upload.

            Inputs: local_path (used only to build the command — the server never
            reads your disk) and content_type.
            Returns: an upload ticket with a ready-to-run upload_command.
            Next: run upload_command locally, confirm it exits 0 (a nonzero exit
            means the PUT failed — do not proceed), then pass the returned
            upload_id to create_simulation inside the asset — a media asset as
            {type:"image", asset: {source:"upload", upload_id}}, or an email
            body image as {type:"email", subject, body_image:
            {source:"upload", upload_id}}. ``label`` is optional on every asset
            — omit it and the server auto-numbers "Option 1", "Option 2", ...

schema.description:
A presigned upload target + a ready-to-run command.

Run ``upload_command`` locally (when present) and confirm it exits 0, then pass ``upload_id``
to create_simulation. If ``expires_at`` lapses first, re-mint via
prepare_asset_upload.
schema.title: AssetUploadTicket

post.summary: Launch a new simulation to test creatives against an audience.
post.description:
Launch a new simulation to test creatives against an audience.
            Call this only AFTER the four decisions are settled and the user has
            confirmed them — objective, assets, template, audience and
            participants, worked ONE QUESTION AT A TIME (see
            get_simulation_options). Use when the user wants to evaluate or test
            something new — "test this copy", "how will Gen-Z react to this
            concept", "compare these three taglines", "run a study on this
            headline", "set up a test for our new campaign". This tool does not
            collect the decisions; it launches what was already agreed.
            Assets can be text, an email, or a media creative
            (image/video/html/audio) — never silently skip a creative the user
            gave you. An asset's TYPE follows what the user is testing, NOT the
            uploaded file's format: when testing emails, an uploaded image is
            that email's body_image (type "email"), not a standalone image
            creative; only make an upload a standalone image when the user is
            testing images. Each asset type attaches differently: a TEXT asset
            is inline copy (no upload, no URL); an EMAIL asset has an inline subject +
            optional preview text, and only its OPTIONAL body image carries bytes;
            a MEDIA asset carries bytes from a public URL (passed straight in) or a
            local file uploaded with prepare_asset_upload / open_asset_upload. Only
            media assets and email body images ever use an upload or URL — do NOT
            call the upload tools for a text asset or an email's subject/preview.
            ALWAYS confirm the input summary with the user before launching —
            an unconditional gate, every time, never skipped or shortened.
            Show EXACTLY these 5 fields: objective, assets, template (its
            title), segment(s) (by name), sample size (the participant
            count). EXPLICITLY OMIT BOTH the population name AND the design
            type (the server determines the design type from the asset
            count). If the user asks to see the summary again, show the SAME
            full 5-field plan, never a shorter one. A run consumes resources.
            Call this ONLY after
            list_workspaces and get_simulation_options — if you have not
            fetched those yet, call them FIRST, then return here.
            These are Adobe Brand Intelligence simulations.

            Inputs: workspace_id is a TOP-LEVEL argument, NOT a field inside
            request — every other field (template_id, name, population_id,
            assets, ...) goes inside request, never beside it. request is a
            SimulationRequest built from get_simulation_options ids.
            Always pass workspace_id explicitly — from list_workspaces,
            defaulting to the one flagged is_active unless the user named a
            different workspace. If omitted it falls back to the active
            workspace, but do not rely on that fallback — pass the id.
            Each asset is a flat object tagged by "type" at the TOP LEVEL —
            {"type": "text", "content": ...}, NOT nested as {"type": "text",
            "text": {...}}. A text asset supplies inline "content"; an email
            asset supplies "subject" (+ optional "preview_text") and an
            optional "body_image"; a media asset (image/video/html/audio) supplies
            an "asset" whose bytes come EITHER from a public url (source="url") the
            server fetches OR an upload_id (source="upload") from
            prepare_asset_upload / open_asset_upload for a local file. Where a
            BinarySource applies (a media asset's "asset" or an email's
            "body_image"), supplying both url and upload_id — or neither — is
            rejected by the schema. "label" is OPTIONAL on every asset — omit it
            and the server auto-numbers unlabeled assets "Option 1", "Option 2",
            ... by position; only set it when you want a specific name shown.
            Assets should be freshly provided for THIS
            simulation — do not reuse a new asset id or url from a prior simulation
            unless the user explicitly requests it. A comparative/sequential_monadic
            design_type needs at least two assets to compare; with fewer, the
            server launches a monadic design instead — mention this to the user
            if they asked for a comparison with only one asset.
            Returns: outcome=launched with the run's ids and webview_url, or
            outcome=draft_incomplete with a webview_url to finish in the tile.
            Next: on outcome=launched, poll get_simulation periodically until
            status is resultsReady/archived AND summary_status is ready — a run
            can reach resultsReady while its summary is still pending, so keep
            polling — then report the executive summary.
            You are the only reporter of results — poll every launch. Some hosts
            also draw a progress panel; it is a decorative visual for the user
            and hands you nothing, so never wait on it instead of polling. On
            outcome=draft_incomplete, send the user to webview_url to finish in
            the tile.

schema.description:
create_simulation result.

``outcome`` is ``launched`` when a run started, or ``draft_incomplete``
when the study was created but a later step failed (the draft is resumable
in the tile via ``webview_url``).
schema.title: CreateSimulationResult

post.summary: Browse or find the user's existing simulations and check their
post.description:
Browse or find the user's existing simulations and check their
            status. Use when the user wants to see what they already have —
            "show me my simulations", "what studies do I have", "list my recent
            runs", "find the one I set up last week", "is the C-Pro test done
            yet". This finds and lists simulations with their status only; it
            does NOT read a simulation's findings (use get_simulation for
            results) and does NOT start anything new (use create_simulation).
            These are Adobe Brand Intelligence simulations.

            This IS how you browse the Adobe Brand Intelligence app — call it directly. Do
            NOT open a web browser or computer-use to view the Adobe Brand Intelligence web
            UI, even when the user says "in / on the simulate app"; that phrasing
            means use this tool.

            Inputs: always pass workspace_id explicitly — from list_workspaces,
            defaulting to the one flagged is_active unless the user named
            a specific workspace or wants to see another. If omitted, this
            falls back to listing the active workspace, but do not rely on
            that fallback — pass the id explicitly.
            Returns: the CURRENT set of simulations in the workspace — each
            simulation's id, name, workspace id, run-aware status, and
            last-updated time. A simulation not present here is not active
            (e.g. archived or removed) — do not supplement this result with
            previously-seen ids. Show the user the simulation name and
            status; keep the ids for tool calls only.
            Next: pass a simulation_id to get_simulation.

schema.description: ``list_simulations`` result — a top-level object, not a bare array.
schema.title: ListSimulationsResult

post.summary: Read and interpret the results of one specific simulation. Use
post.description:
Read and interpret the results of one specific simulation. Use
            when the user asks about the findings of a simulation — "how did
            version B do", "what did the audience say about the C-Pro test",
            "summarize the results of my last run", "show me the transcripts",
            "which creative won". First resolve WHICH simulation they mean: if
            the reference is ambiguous or matches several, list candidates with
            list_simulations and ask before reading. Read-only — this does not
            start or change a run. Lead with the top-line summary and surface
            confidence: if a result is low-confidence or the engine abstained,
            say so plainly rather than presenting a score as certain. If the
            simulation isn't finished, say it's still running rather than
            reporting empty results. Also returns a link to open it in the
            Adobe Brand Intelligence web app.

            Inputs: workspace_id and simulation_id (both from list_simulations).
            Returns: status, inputs, webview_url, and summary_status.
            inputs describes what the simulation was configured with: objective,
            design_type, participants (sample size), population and segments (by
            name), dimensions being measured (by name), and uploaded assets
            (label + type). Empty segments means the whole population; empty
            dimensions means all scored dimensions; inputs fields are empty for a
            draft that has not been fully configured yet.
            summary_status is one of not_ready (no finished run yet), ready
            (summary fetched), or pending (run finished but the summary isn't
            available yet — retry shortly).
            Next: if summary_status is pending, retry shortly; if ready, read
            executive_summary.

schema.description:
``get_simulation`` result.

``summary_status`` distinguishes the three valid states of the executive
summary: ``not_ready`` (no ready run yet), ``ready`` (fetched, possibly an
empty summary), and ``pending`` (run is ready but the summary fetch failed
and should be retried).

thumbnails.description: stimulusId -> 1-hour presigned thumbnail URL. Empty dict when the study has no image stimuli or the fetch fails. Rides in structuredContent so the panel can build a thumbnailFor resolver. Each URL is itself a bearer capability (not just data) valid for 1 hour, and, like `analysis`, is serialized verbatim into the tool's model-facing text content on every get_simulation call — not only into the panel.
thumbnails.title: Thumbnails

contents.description: stimulusId -> the stimulus's own text content (the concept copy for text stimuli; empty for stimuli that carry no text, e.g. images). Empty dict on failure. Rides in structuredContent so the panel can build a contentFor resolver, and, like `thumbnails`/`analysis`, is also serialized into the tool's model-facing text content on every get_simulation call.
contents.title: Contents

schema.title: SimulationDetail

AssetInput.description: An uploaded asset (stimulus) as label + type.
AssetInput.title: AssetInput

EmailAsset.description:
An email stimulus. ``subject`` and ``preview_text`` are inline text (no
upload). ``body_image`` is OPTIONAL and is the only part that carries bytes —
supply it (public url or a local-file upload_id) only when the email has a
body image; leave it out for a subject/preview-only email.

label.description: Optional short name shown for this creative in results (e.g. 'Version A'). Omit it — the server auto-numbers unlabeled assets as 'Option 1', 'Option 2', ... by their position in the assets list.
label.title: Label

subject.description: Email subject line — inline text, required.
subject.title: Subject

preview_text.description: Optional inbox preview/pre-header text — inline text, no upload.
preview_text.title: Preview Text

body_image.description: Optional email body image — the only part of an email that carries bytes. Public url, or an upload_id from prepare_asset_upload / open_asset_upload for a local file. Omit for a text-only email.
body_image.title: Body Image

EmailAsset.title: EmailAsset

ExecutiveSummary.description: The ``{summary, recommendations}`` block from a finished run.
ExecutiveSummary.title: ExecutiveSummary

MediaAsset.description:
A binary creative — image / video / html / audio. Its bytes come from a
``BinarySource``: a public ``url`` the server fetches, or an ``upload`` staged
from a local file via prepare_asset_upload / open_asset_upload. This is the
only TOP-LEVEL asset whose payload is binary; the only other bytes are an
``EmailAsset``'s optional ``body_image``.

label.description: Optional short name shown for this creative in results (e.g. 'Version A'). Omit it — the server auto-numbers unlabeled assets as 'Option 1', 'Option 2', ... by their position in the assets list.
label.title: Label

asset.description: Where the creative's bytes come from — a public url the server fetches, or an upload_id for a local file staged via prepare_asset_upload / open_asset_upload.
asset.title: Asset

MediaAsset.title: MediaAsset

NamedRef.description: An id paired with its resolved display name (``None`` when unresolved).
NamedRef.title: NamedRef

Simulation.description: One simulation (backend ``study``) in a workspace listing.
Simulation.title: Simulation

SimulationInputs.description:
What a simulation was configured with, in a legible (name-resolved) form.

Empty ``segments`` means the whole population is eligible; empty
``dimensions`` means all of the questionnaire's scored dimensions. Fields
degrade to their default when the backing fetch is missing or fails.
SimulationInputs.title: SimulationInputs

SimulationRequest.description:
What the simulation is, after the user has confirmed inputs.

Which workspace it lands in is a separate top-level ``create_simulation``
argument (optional — omitted means the caller's active workspace), matching
list_simulations / get_simulation.

questionnaire_id.description: Explicit questionnaire id to measure against (from get_simulation_options / the list_questionnaires CLI). Omit to resolve from the template. Pass the tenant's full-coverage questionnaire to measure all its metrics.
questionnaire_id.title: Questionnaire Id

name.description: Name for the simulation, shown to the user.
name.title: Name

objective.description: What the simulation should find out, in the user's own framing. Defaults to the template's objective when omitted.
objective.title: Objective

segment_ids.description: Segment ids to target within the population. EMPTY means the whole population — only leave it empty when the user wants everyone.
segment_ids.title: Segment Ids

sample_size.description: Number of simulated respondents. Omit to use the template's default; the user may ask for more or fewer.
sample_size.title: Sample Size

assets.description: The creatives to test — one tagged entry per stimulus the user gave you (text, email, or media). Never silently skip one.
assets.title: Assets

design_type.description: One of the template's allowed design types (e.g. 'monadic', 'sequential_monadic'). A comparative/sequential_monadic design needs at least two assets to compare; when fewer are supplied, the server uses a monadic design instead.
design_type.title: Design Type

brand_name.description: Brand the creatives belong to, when the user names one.
brand_name.title: Brand Name

run_name.description: Optional label for this particular run of the simulation.
run_name.title: Run Name

SimulationRequest.title: SimulationRequest

dimensions.description: Informational only — what this template measures, for showing the user. NOT an input to create_simulation; there is no dimensions field on its request.
dimensions.title: Dimensions

TextAsset.description:
An inline text stimulus — plain copy, e.g. a headline or tagline. There is
NO file and NO URL: put the text in ``content``. Never call
prepare_asset_upload / open_asset_upload for a text asset.

label.description: Optional short name shown for this creative in results (e.g. 'Version A'). Omit it — the server auto-numbers unlabeled assets as 'Option 1', 'Option 2', ... by their position in the assets list.
label.title: Label

content.description: The text copy itself, inline — not a URL or file.
content.title: Content

TextAsset.title: TextAsset

UploadSource.description:
Bytes the client already staged for a LOCAL file. Get the ``upload_id``
from prepare_asset_upload (when you have a readable path) or open_asset_upload
(when you do not) — never invent one.

upload_id.description: upload_id returned by prepare_asset_upload / open_asset_upload after the local file's bytes were staged.
upload_id.title: Upload Id

content_type.description: Ignored. Not required — the upload path only needs upload_id. Accepted because prepare_asset_upload's ticket returns content_type and callers naturally pass it through.
content_type.title: Content Type

UploadSource.title: UploadSource

UrlSource.description:
Bytes the server fetches over HTTPS — use for a creative that already
lives at a public URL. No upload step: the server downloads it itself.

url.description: Public HTTPS URL the server fetches the bytes from.
url.title: Url

UrlSource.title: UrlSource
